input.quote: 13.6.1 Governing Law. This Agreement or the performance, enforcement, breach or termination hereof shall be interpreted, governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, United States, excluding any conflicts or choice of law rule or principle that might otherwise refer construction or interpretation of this Agreement to the substantive law of another jurisdiction
input.rationale: Section 13.6.1 selects Delaware law, which sits squarely at the playbook fallback (Delaware law is an accepted jurisdiction), so no redline is warranted. Dispute resolution under Section 13.7 is a senior-officer escalation followed by an optional election to arbitrate under Schedule 13.7.3, with IP validity/enforceability/patentability disputes expressly carved out for litigation in courts of competent jurisdiction (13.7.2) and inventorship referred to a USPTO-registered attorney under U.S. patent law (13.7.2). Nothing imposes a foreign forum, so the walk-away trigger (vendor home jurisdiction outside the accepted list, or mandatory arbitration seated abroad) is not engaged. Two minor sub-elements are noted rather than flagged: the arbitration seat and rules are contained in Schedule 13.7.3, whose text is redacted ([***]), and Section 13.6 contains no express jurisdiction sub-clause even though 13.6.2 (service) refers to "any such court". On diligence we should confirm the Schedule 13.7.3 seat is in the United States; if it turns out to be a foreign seat, this rule would need to be re-run as a deviation.
